_meta.purpose: Fund-lifecycle events on a timeline, anchored to the district ledger, grouped into story chains. The atomic unit of the news/timeline layer. See news-timeline-schema.md.
_meta.rules: Same sourcing discipline as the ledger: every event carries a source + tier and a confidence (documented = gov source / reported = news only / alleged). amount_cr stays null unless PDF-cited (figure_gap). No event is fabricated; seeds are real, ledger-anchored stories.
_meta.coverage: 2 seed story chains (Birbhum MGNREGS freeze; Kolkata KMC grant dependency). Built to be extended by ingest_news.py + human anchoring.
_meta.scheme_ref_note: scheme_ref resolves against district-ledger.json _meta.scheme_registry / scheme_aliases. official_ref resolves against the district roster role keys + _meta.authority_map.
_meta.accountability_chain: Each story_chain can carry the full accountability arc: promise -> result -> actual_cost -> human_impact. This is the 'source vs bias vs stated promise vs result vs actual (per-capita) cost' unit. Rules that keep it defensible:

accountability_rules.promise: The political entity's OWN stated commitment ONLY (manifesto / budget speech / scheme launch / official release), QUOTED with a source URL. We never infer motive or 'agenda' — we quote what was promised and cite it. entity = the body that made the promise (govt/ministry/party as stated in the source), never an accusation.
accountability_rules.result: What is documented to have happened, sourced. Factual (delivered / delayed / withheld / lapsed), never a verdict.
accountability_rules.actual_cost: Total amount_cr AND per_capita_inr, EACH cited. per_capita = amount / Census-2011 population at the stated scope (district or state). scope MUST be labelled — never pass a state figure off as per-district. figure_gap=true until the amount is sourced.
accountability_rules.human_impact: Plain-language, factual statement of what this meant for residents (what was denied or delivered) — 'human value, not economic contribution'. No adjectives of blame; state the concrete effect.
accountability_rules.social_line: A ready-to-post one-liner (<=200 chars) for auto social posting (share.html / post_to_social.py). Facts + figure + source-implied, never an accusation.

_meta.per_capita_note: per_capita_inr is rupees per resident (amount_cr * 1e7 / population). Population from district-pop.json (Census 2011). Scope 'state' uses the summed state population; 'district' uses the district population. Shown to make cost HUMAN and comparable, not to assert contribution.

story_chains.title: Birbhum's MGNREGS money: frozen at the top for four years
story_chains.one_line: Centre froze WB's MGNREGS funds under Sec 27 (Mar 2022); ₹3,038 cr dues piled up; resumed Jun 2026 after Supreme Court intervention. Dysfunction = money WITHHELD upstream, not misspent.

promise.stated: MGNREGA guarantees at least 100 days of wage employment in a financial year to every rural household whose adults volunteer to do unskilled manual work.

result.stated: Fund release to West Bengal was frozen from 9 Mar 2022 under Sec 27; no MGNREGS wages flowed to WB districts for ~4 years until a June 2026 resumption after Supreme Court intervention.

actual_cost.amount_note: Centre-stated pending MGNREGS dues to WB (Rajya Sabha, 2025) — the withheld amount, not district-split.
actual_cost.per_capita_note: ₹3,038 cr ÷ WB Census-2011 population — ₹333 of guaranteed-wage money withheld per WB resident (state scope; NOT Birbhum-specific).

source.title: Centre owes ₹3,000 crore MGNREGA dues to Bengal (Rajya Sabha)

story_chains.human_impact: The statutory job guarantee stopped functioning in WB's rural districts: households that would have earned MGNREGS wages did not, unbuilt assets and reported distress migration followed. ~₹333 of guaranteed-wage money per resident sat withheld upstream.
story_chains.social_line: West Bengal's MGNREGS job-guarantee funds were frozen by the Centre for ~4 years — ₹3,038 cr in dues, ~₹333 per resident withheld — until the Supreme Court pushed a June 2026 restart. [sourced]

story_chains.title: Kolkata's civic money: over half flows down as grant
story_chains.one_line: KMC's BE 2025-26 shows ₹2,897 cr of ₹5,525 cr receipts are Central+State grant — 52% grant-dependent, budget in deficit.

promise.stated: KMC's Budget Estimate 2025-26 projects total receipts of ₹5,524.84 cr to fund the city's civic services for the year.

result.stated: Of ₹5,524.84 cr total receipts, ₹2,897 cr (~52%) is Central + State Grant-in-Aid rather than locally raised revenue; the budget is in deficit.

actual_cost.amount_note: Central + State grant component of KMC's BE 2025-26 receipts (the money that flows DOWN rather than being raised locally).
actual_cost.per_capita_note: ₹2,897 cr ÷ Kolkata Census-2011 population — ₹6,443 of the city's per-resident civic money comes from grant, not local revenue.

story_chains.human_impact: For every Kolkata resident, about ₹6,443 of the year's civic spending depends on grant money flowing down from the Centre and State — so local services are exposed to how reliably that upstream money arrives.
story_chains.social_line: 52% of Kolkata's ₹5,525 cr civic budget is grant, not locally raised — ~₹6,443 per resident depends on money flowing down from above. [KMC BE 2025-26, gov PDF]

fiscal_events.title: Centre freezes MGNREGS fund release to West Bengal (Sec 27)
fiscal_events.summary: The Union stopped MGNREGS fund release to West Bengal from 9 March 2022 under Section 27 of the MGNREGA Act, citing non-compliance/corruption. Every MGNREGS-dependent district, including Birbhum, was cut off from wages at source.

fiscal_events.title: Pending MGNREGS dues to WB reach ₹3,038 cr (highest of any state)
fiscal_events.summary: Per the Centre's figure in the Rajya Sabha (2025), pending MGNREGS dues to West Bengal stood at ₹3,038 cr — the highest of any state. The state claims ₹18,000 cr across MGNREGS + PMAY-G. Rural districts like Birbhum bore the brunt: assets unbuilt, migration.

fiscal_events.title: KMC budget: ₹2,897 cr of ₹5,525 cr receipts are Central+State grant
fiscal_events.summary: Kolkata Municipal Corporation's Budget Estimate 2025-26 records a 'Government Grant' (Central + State Grant-in-Aid) of ₹2,897 cr against total receipts of ₹5,524.84 cr — about 52% of the city's civic money flows down as grant, not raised locally. The budget is in deficit.
